title: Mocks II, 100-problem review list, capstone blog post
objective: Keep the mock cadence; build the final 100-problem high-signal review list from your mistake log; write the engineering blog post; deploy the capstone on your own domain.
topics: Engineering blog post: what broke, what you measured, what you would change
Interview logistics: debrief ritual, scheduling, energy
theory: Google M12; reference CI-1 writeup habit.
deliverables: review/top100.md (problem, pattern, gap type, last cold-solve date)
Capstone live on your domain with <₹500/month run cost documented
checkpoint: Blog post read by 3 engineers who give harsh feedback

knowledge: Which 10 problems on top100 scare you most?
What did the 3 reviewers call weakest?
practical: Blog post published; capstone on your domain

tasks.text: Coding mock 1, recorded; debrief; drill the gap.
review/top100.md: from mistakes.md, pick the 100 highest-signal problems (misses, slow solves, company skew: Google graphs/DP); schedule cold re-solves across W50–W52.

Engineering blog post on one flagship (AtlasAI or Paper-to-Prod): the problem, architecture, what broke, what you measured (tables), what you would change. 1,200–1,800 words; diagrams; honest limitations.
Cold re-solves: 5 from top100.
Quiet Network: 1–2 genuine conversations with engineers from your target list (thoughtful comment or a question about their work; no pitch, no referral ask). Log in the tracker.
System-design mock (45 min): software case (job scheduler or payment workflow). Record; delta.
Capstone: deploy on your own domain (DNS, TLS, CDN for static, API behind spend cap); document run cost.
10-min recall: explain yesterday’s “Capstone: deploy on your own domain (DNS, TLS, CDN for static, API behind spend cap); docu” aloud without notes; write one gap you found.
Send the blog draft to 3 engineers: “tell me the weakest part of this”. Incorporate; publish. Share on LinkedIn.
Cold re-solves: 5 from top100 + 1 timed set.
Quiet Network: 1–2 genuine conversations with engineers from your target list (thoughtful comment or a question about their work; no pitch, no referral ask). Log in the tracker.
Coding mock 2, recorded; debrief; drill the gap.
Interview logistics: post-round debrief template (which stage wobbled; which pattern; drill plan), scheduling rules (no back-to-back loops), sleep/energy plan.
Application pipeline (20 min): check saved searches, apply to 1–2 fitting roles within 48 h of posting, update tracker (status · next action · what failed).
Watch this week’s mocks; update the failure patterns list; verify last week’s fixes landed.
Applications: follow-ups + 5 new; tracker; log rejection reasons as course-correction data.

Weekly revision — Mocks: 2 coding + 1 SD, Final 100-problem high-signal review list (weakness-driven), Engineering blog post: what broke, what you measured, what you would change, Capstone deployed on your domain: rewrite the key ideas from memory (no notes), then compare with your notes and fix the gaps. Reimplement two things from this week without looking.
DSA second pass · cold re-solve: Maximum Product Subarray (Medium, B75) · Word Break (Medium, B75) — ≤35 min each, narrate, log time.
Weekly review: answer this week’s knowledge questions aloud, run the practical checks, then write the three notes (struggled / learned / improve) in Weekly Plan → Review. Update the tracking sheet.

JS/MERN spaced recall (Cycle 3 · interview mode) · React advanced: hooks, performance, data fetching: Interview mode: implement an autocomplete with debounce + AbortController + keyboard nav in 25 min. Log misses in mistakes.md; if you fail the check, redo the matching module in Side Tracks → 🟨 JavaScript & MERN Refresher.
Plan next week: read W51’s objective and Day 1; move any unfinished 🔴 task into next week’s Day 1; confirm calendar blocks. Then rest — consistency beats intensity.
